She kept his shaving brush in the medicine cabinet. He was on a long work trip. The bristles had stiffened.
Her cousin's recipe binder lay on the kitchen shelf. The marmalade page was open from her batch last week.
He still kept her old pair of scissors on the desk. They were the sharpest pair in the house.
She kept her brother's college sweatshirt folded in the linen closet. She borrowed it on cold weekends.
His father's coin jar was on the dresser. The coins inside were from his end-of-day pocket emptying.
She kept his cane in the hallway umbrella stand. He used it after the knee surgery. The rubber tip had worn.
Her son's lacrosse stick sat in the garage. He was between practices. The pocket stood strung the way he liked.
He still kept her bottle of lavender oil on the bathroom shelf. The cap was loose from her use last night.
His brother's nameplate was on the office door. The building manager had not gotten around to changing it.
She kept his old pair of work gloves on the workbench. He wore them for his weekend mason jobs.
Her grandmother's tea cozy sat on the kettle. The pattern was knitted in a stitch she had taught the family.
He kept her embroidery hoop on the side table. The half-finished stitch was a leaf in green floss.
His son's bike lock combination was on a sticky note in his wallet. The bike lay at the rack for the semester.
She kept his glasses case in the bedside drawer. The case was empty during the day. He used the glasses for reading.
Her father's checkbook sat in the desk drawer. The next check was numbered for the lumber order.
He kept his mother's wedding band on a chain in the dresser. The chain was knotted from a recent untangling.
Her sister's straw hat sat on the hook by the back door. The brim was bent down where her hand grabbed it.
His friend's hiking poles were in the closet. They had walked a red-clay trail last weekend together.
She kept her son's first tooth in a small envelope in the jewelry box. Her younger handwriting was on the front.
